decisions.note: Round 3 prototype derived only a domain-based name (e.g. 'Nytimes') instead of fetching the real page title; client explicitly asked for the actual headline, and maker corrected it in round 4 (fetches real title).

Round 5 search prototype only matches title and site address (live substring filter); no full-text over description/note, no #tag syntax, no AND/OR/NOT/parentheses, no quoted-phrase exact match — client affirmed 'that covers what I'd reach for,' a satisficing miss that persisted unchanged through the round-13 acceptance.

Round 6 offered folders (single-category, would contradict the many-to-many tag model), tags (matches reference), and automatic (no reference basis); client selected Tags specifically because a link can carry multiple labels, matching the reference's many-to-many tag design.

Round 9 duplicate-save handling only highlights/points to the existing bookmark ('Show me the one I saved') rather than guiding the user into editing it, as the reference requires; client called it 'a nice touch' and never caught the gap, which persisted through the round-13 acceptance test.
